description: §6.7.3 — the two LEGITIMATE cleanup() forms in one file: an arrow expression `cleanup(() => { teardown() })` and a bare function reference `cleanup(teardown)`. This is the FALSE-POSITIVE guard for the S310 diagnostics: the checks are newly-rejecting, so the shapes adopters actually write must stay clean.
rationale: §6.7.3 sanctions both the arrow form and the function-reference form. The S310 checker is deliberately conservative — it fires only on shapes that CANNOT be functions (`lit`/`array`/`object`) plus the explicit call-expression case — because a false positive breaks working adopter code while a missed case merely preserves prior behaviour.
